title: TypeScript
description: Gates for a TypeScript or JavaScript repo. Each tool comes from the repo's node_modules, so its version is the one the lockfile pins.

gates.description: Lints the changed files with ESLint, warnings included: a warning nobody is sent back for is never fixed.

Type-checks the project with tsc, since a change in one file can break the types of another, and writes no JavaScript. Incremental: tsc keeps what it learnt under node_modules/.cache and re-checks only what the changed files reach. Refused when tsconfig.json only references others, as in an Angular project, since tsc would check no file: give it -p and a tsconfig.
Checks that Prettier leaves the changed files as they are.
Runs only the Vitest tests that import a changed file, directly or not.

Runs only the node:test tests that import a changed file, directly or not, for a repo that tests with Node itself. Node has no related mode: the helper follows the imports. It finds the tests by Node's own naming; --tests <regex> narrows it, and --require-tests also fails on a changed file no test reaches, which the related tests alone pass in silence.
Fails on the copy-pasted blocks the turn added, never on the ones already there. An agent that misses an existing helper writes a second one, and the two drift apart.

Type-checks the project with strictNullChecks and strictPropertyInitialization on, and fails only on the errors the turn added: a project that turned them off, with more errors than it can fix at once, stops growing new ones. An error is told by its file, code and source line, since tsc prints the types of a message otherwise from one compilation to the next: one a change moves to another line is not new, nor one tsc reports in another file with the same message, nor one on a line the turn changed, as long as its file has no more errors of its code than at the turn start. The agent still reads the message. tsc keeps watching between turns; without the watch, it runs at each prompt and stop instead. Refused when tsconfig.json only references others, as in an Angular project, since tsc would check no file: give it -p and a tsconfig. The whole check counts every error.
Fails on the unused files, exports and dependencies the turn added, never on the ones already there, so it works on a repo that already has some.

Fails on the rule suppressions the turn added, never on the ones already there: eslint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, @ts-nocheck, prettier-ignore, biome-ignore. The cheapest green is to silence the rule, and this is the gate that refuses it.
